flawed_step: 0078: Pairing the ith bipartite cover on X with the ith cover on Y produces k-1 bipartite graphs, not 2^{k-1} bipartite graphs. There are only k-1 indices to pair.
counterexample: Take k=2 and n=4, with X={1,2} and Y={3,4}. By the k-1=1 case, K_X is covered by the single bipartite graph H_X having edge 12, and K_Y by the single bipartite graph H_Y having edge 34. Pairing graphs with the same index produces exactly one graph H_X∪H_Y, the matching with edges {12,34}; it is bipartite. Step 0078 claims this operation produces 2^{k-1}=2 graphs, but the explicit pairing has only one index and therefore only one resulting graph.
assessment_summary: The argument is justified through step 0072 (with the duplicated |X| and occurrences of k-l in the quoted proof understood as evident typographical errors for |Y| and k-1). The first definite mathematical error is the graph count in step 0078. The intended count is k-1; adding the X–Y biclique then gives k graphs total.
